status: constructed; all adopted numerical evidence reconciled in one probability law
scientific_rationale: The OLS normal equations with the original adjustment sets recover the outcome-predictor covariances. The two reports agree on Cov(Z,Y). A positive-definite predictor covariance matrix then uniquely determines the joint OLS coefficients, and the reported outcome variance determines the remaining residual variance. A joint Gaussian law realizes these compatible first and second moments.
assumptions: The full law is multivariate Gaussian; the reports identify moments but do not identify a distribution family.
The conditional outcome mean is linear and its residual is independent, Gaussian, and homoscedastic. These properties extend beyond the reported OLS summaries.
Generated rows are iid from P0. The population reports are exact inputs rather than uncertain sample estimates.
Finite generated cohorts fluctuate around the reported population statistics; no sample-moment calibration is imposed.

deterministic_consistency_calculations.normal_equations: c_A = Sigma_[Z,X1] beta_A; c_B = Sigma_[Z,X2] beta_B; shared Cov(Z,Y) must agree.
deterministic_consistency_calculations.joint_OLS_equation: beta = inverse(Sigma_predictors) c; intercept = mean_Y - mean_predictors dot beta.
